original.target_description: Study 4: between-subject college-transfer scenario, association between temporal perspective and choice of action Jim versus inaction Dave as experiencing greater regret. This is hypothetical regret, not reported regret for participants’ own lives.

n.sample_role: Cornell undergraduate participants: 34 in short-term condition and 42 in long-term condition; both groups enter the association test.
n.quote:
of the 34 subjects who were asked whether Dave or Jim would
experience more regret in the short-term ... 62% of the 42 subjects who were asked about
the long run

replication.target_description: Study 4: between-subject hypothetical college-transfer scenario, chi-square association of temporal distance with action versus inaction regret. This is not a comparison of respondents’ personal lifetime regrets.

n.sample_role: Post-exclusion participants randomized to the between-subject scenario study, both temporal-distance conditions.
n.exclusions: Post-exclusion study group; 29 excluded from combined 1017. Study-specific exclusion counts not printed in main text.

reported_success.location: Comparing Replication Findings to Original Findings and Extensions; Table 6
reported_success.quote: We successfully replicated and found support for the original findings in Studies 1, 3, and 4 (short-term regret and temporal effect) with smaller effect sizes.

notes: Locator discrepancy: supplied Study 4 identifies a hypothetical scenario and temporal association, whereas the neutral description refers to reported regret for life’s inactions versus actions (the Study 1a outcome). Both target_match values are false. Retained the Study 4 temporal-association tests, without substituting the Study 1a test or assuming a lifetime-only condition. Original condition sizes retained separately without calculating an aggregate. Original chi-square and p visually verified against the downloaded primary paper page image; cached extracted text omits that line.
